title: Tennr and OpenAI: Advancing Computer Use for Prior Authorization
summary: Tennr and OpenAI announced a partnership on Nov. 16. Together, the companies will push prior authorization workflows forward by deploying computer-using agents to authorization tasks. Tennr's same deep expertise in provider workflows and payer standards, made more powerful by OpenAI's frontier models.
body_markdown:
Tennr is partnering with OpenAI to evaluate computer-using agents for prior authorization workflows. Computer-use agents (CUA) autonomously complete tasks in software by reading screens, clicking, typing, and navigating between applications.


However, having the ability to work within and between systems doesn’t guarantee agents will complete tasks correctly. Especially in a field as complex and demanding as healthcare, CUAs must be armed with sufficient context to make proper decisions.


That’s where Tennr comes in.


We supply the patient and insurance context that allows agents to work effectively. With Tennr, agents can navigate payer portals, enter information, submit supporting records, retrieve decisions, and return them directly to your team’s workflow.


All of this work happens while maintaining proper application access controls, audit logs, and human-review requirements, for transparent workflows you can trace and trust.


Tennr’s pilot, announced Nov. 16, compares agent execution of prior auth with staff-performed work, assessing whether required steps are completed accurately and consistently. This is the beginning of leveraging automation to its full potential: frontier models powered by specialized insights, for fast decisions that feel like they came from a member of your team.


### **Why Prior Authorization**


Tennr is focusing first on prior authorization because it comes with substantial administrative complexity and the outcomes have direct consequences for patient access.


Prior authorization has historically been onerous: requirements vary by payer and treatment, and staff must often work across systems to assemble documentation, submit requests, monitor responses, and act on decisions.


Limited transparency complicates the problem further. The AMA’s review of 15 Medicare Advantage contracts identified disclosures[behind password-protected portals](https://www.ama-assn.org/practice-management/prior-authorization/making-payers-prior-authorization-data-easier-access) , procedure-code lists without plain-language descriptions, and incomplete or internally inconsistent statistics.


Despite providers’ focus on improving prior auth processes, denials remain rampant.


KFF’s 2025 analysis of[prior auth outcomes](https://www.kff.org/patient-consumer-protections/prior-authorization-metrics-provide-new-insights-into-insurer-practices-but-gaps-remain/) for large insurers found average standard-request denial rates of 12% in Medicare Advantage, 14% in Medicaid managed care, and 18% in the Affordable Care Act Marketplace. What’s more, among appealed denials, 67%, 47%, and 43%, respectively, were overturned.


This suggests that many first-pass denials may be inappropriate and underscores the importance of building workflows that can resubmit and track authorizations to completion. Submitting a prior authorization once is not enough to ensure timely care access.


### **What CUA Advancements Mean for Healthcare**


Effective computer use can move healthcare AI from interpreting information to executing the administrative tasks that follow.


Our partnership comes as[OpenAI makes a broader push](https://openai.com/index/more-ways-to-move-care-forward-with-chatgpt-for-healthcare/) to advance computer use for healthcare. Tennr’s collaboration with OpenAI lets us extend model research while meeting rigorous operational requirements. The objective is to help advance the underlying capabilities while developing the surrounding systems needed to make them useful in healthcare. Demonstrating reliable execution here is the next step toward determining whether computer-using agents can reduce administrative work and support more timely patient access.


To learn more about how Tennr is working on the frontier of patient access,[book time with us](http://tennr.com/book-a-demo) .
